Content:
Adding or subtracting a value to the graph of [MATH: y=\left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^x] will translate (shift) the graph up or down the [MATH: y]-axis.

Content:
For instance, [MATH: y=\left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^x+3] has the same shape as [MATH: y=\left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^x,] but it's shifted [MATH: 3] units up.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/72716eb23ad3000031ce534baa96c863]

Content:
Note the following points:

Content:
- The [MATH: y]-intercept [MATH: (0,1)] has moved up [MATH: 3] units to the point [MATH: (0,4).]
- The horizontal asymptote [MATH: y=0] has moved up [MATH: 3] units to [MATH: y=3.]

Content:

sections.normalized_html: The graph below shows the curve [MATH: y = k\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}+c.] Determine the values of [MATH: k] and [MATH: c] and find the equation of the curve.
sections.readable_text:
The graph below shows the curve [MATH: y = k\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}+c.] Determine the values of [MATH: k] and [MATH: c] and find the equation of the curve.

[IMG: /graphics/d8f79039924340963dd585e4535b185a]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The horizontal asymptote of the curve [MATH: y=k\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}+c] is [MATH: y=c.] In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is [MATH: y=-5], hence [MATH: c=-5.]

We can solve for [MATH: k] by finding a point on the graph and substituting for [MATH: x] and [MATH: y.] The labeled point on the graph is [MATH: (0,-1),] so we substitute [MATH: x=0] and [MATH: y=-1] into the function and solve for [MATH: k\mathbin{:}] [MATH: k((1)/(2))^{x} + c|= y; k((1)/(2))^{x} − 5|= y; k((1)/(2))^{0} − 5|= − 1; k − 5|= − 1; k|= 4]

Therefore, the equation of the curve is [MATH: y = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x} - 5.]
sections.readable_text:

Therefore, the equation of the curve is [MATH: y = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x} - 5.]

[IMG: /graphics/d8f79039924340963dd585e4535b185a]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The horizontal asymptote of the curve [MATH: y=k\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}+c] is [MATH: y=c.] In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is [MATH: y=-5], hence [MATH: c=-5.]

We can solve for [MATH: k] by finding a point on the graph and substituting for [MATH: x] and [MATH: y.] The labeled point on the graph is [MATH: (0,-1),] so we substitute [MATH: x=0] and [MATH: y=-1] into the function and solve for [MATH: k\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: k((1)/(2))^{x} + c|= y; k((1)/(2))^{x} − 5|= y; k((1)/(2))^{0} − 5|= − 1; k − 5|= − 1; k|= 4]

Therefore, the equation of the curve is [MATH: y = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x} - 5.]
